title: Bandwidth-aware tenant routing and hosted spillover circuit-breakers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Several tenants pinned to Dedicated pools emit high token/s bursts that cause excessive spillover to Hosted. When many tenants spill at once the hosted backstop saturates, increasing latencies and failing SLOs for non-spilling tenants. We need a routing controller that is aware of bandwidth (tokens/sec and requests/sec), tenant priority, and token budgets, plus circuit-breaker safeguards to prevent cascading failure across Dedicated -> Hosted spillover.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable per-tenant token budget enforced at Dedicated cutover with fallback to hosted only when below budget
Circuit-breaker rules that stop spillover when Hosted region-wide token/sec or 95th percentile latency breach configurable thresholds
Routing controller exposes a 'degrade' action: route to lower-cost quantized variant or queued retry window instead of immediate spillover
Canary rollout plan: 5% tenants in us-west-2 for 72 hours with telemetry showing no regressions in tail latency or error rate
Automated unit + integration tests simulating 100 tenants bursting concurrently with expected graceful degradation
Observability dashboards: per-tenant token burn, spillover events, circuit-breaker tripped timeline, and rollback tool in Console
tasks: Design doc: bandwidth-aware routing state machine (Aisha) - include token accounting API and TTL semantics
Routing controller implementation: token budgets, priority weights, and circuit-breaker evaluation (Marco)
Integrate with autoscaler: expose advisory signals to Dedicated autoscaler to pre-warm capacity
Fallback policies: map tenant -> model variant table (full model, quantized, condensed) and implement routing hooks
Telemetry: add token/sec metrics per tenant, spillover_count, circuit_breaker_status; wire to Console dashboards
E2E chaos test: simulate cross-region outage and mass spillover to hosted to validate CB triggers
Docs: runbook for SREs and guide for customers to set tenant token budgets and priority tiers
decisions: Use token/sec + request/sec hybrid metric for bandwidth accounting instead of only TPS to prioritize expensive requests
Circuit-breaker evaluates both absolute hosted capacity (tokens/sec) and relative degradation (p99 latency delta) before tripping
On CB trip, prefer deterministic fallback to a quantized model variant over indiscriminate throttling to preserve best-effort availability
Rate limiter enforcement point will be at the edge routing proxy to minimize cross-service auth overhead
notes: Trade-offs: tighter per-tenant budgets reduce hosted costs but increase user-facing degradation for aggressive tenants
Alternative considered: purely tenant-weighted spillover queue. Rejected because it still allows Hosted saturation during systemic bursts
We should keep the CB cooldown window conservative (initially 60s) and provide ops knobs for shrink/expand during incidents
Potential perf impact: token accounting adds O(1) checks and requires careful batching to avoid per-request latency tax
